Lesson No. 247 at a Glance

This is the first lesson of this surah. Its subject is the question of resurrection after death (ba'th ba'd al-mawt). The polytheists of Makkah denied it, and even those who believed in resurrection were astonished that these people held such a belief. But the Qur'an does not take only their mistaken notion as its subject of discussion. It criticizes their denial as a whole, and seeks to reform them and correct their crooked thinking, so as to bring them back to the path of truth. The aim of the Noble Qur'an is to shake their heedless hearts and awaken them thoroughly, so that they open the doors of their hearts to understand the great truths that lie within this universe. Therefore the Qur'an does not engage them in a debate on the subject of resurrection merely in the style of logical argument. It only revives their dead hearts, polishes their rust-covered minds so that they employ reflection, and touches their intuition so that within it the sense becomes sharp and they can be directly affected by the realities found in their surroundings. This is a lesson from which those whose task is the reform of hearts can benefit greatly.

The surah begins with the letter Qaf and an oath by the Qur'an. The meaning is that this Qur'an is composed of letters of exactly this kind, and the first letter of the word Qur'an is itself qaf.

*****

Here it is not mentioned what the oath is being sworn upon. This oath is at the beginning of the speech. Its first meaning is that Allah is beginning His speech with an oath, so awaken yourselves, the matter is extraordinary. Allah and an oath: therefore the matter is grave. Perhaps the purpose of this opening is precisely this, because instead of mentioning afterwards the matter for which the oath is being sworn, the particle of retraction "bal" (بل) has been brought. Since the oath has already made a strong impression on the addressee, the subject now taken up is their astonishment and the regarding of resurrection after death as an "unheard-of thing," in the manner that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke to the polytheists about being raised again, they denied it as though, in the eyes of the disbelievers, this were a new matter.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 50, verse 2:

"Rather, they are amazed that a warner has come to them from among themselves. So the disbelievers said: 'This is a strange thing! When we die and become dust (will we be raised again)? That return is far beyond reason.'" (50:2–3)

Can it be considered strange that a warner has come to them from among themselves? There is nothing strange in it. Rather, it is entirely a natural matter, and sound human nature accepts it with simplicity and gladness. It is most reasonable that a reformer of a people should be from among them: that he should share their feelings, be one of them, possess their understanding, speak their language, and share in their life, their striving, and their sorrows and pains; that he should know their inclinations and emotions, and know their strength and endurance. Thus he can tell them that the shirk, injustice and wrongdoing in which they are involved will bring a very evil end upon them, and so that he can teach them how to take the straight path, and what changes they must bring about in themselves if they accept the new call. In these changes, duties and responsibilities, he will be the first person, and he will be among them.

They themselves were amazed by prophethood. Then, when a messenger came, he began to place greater emphasis in his call on the belief in resurrection after death, because the whole Islamic system depends on the belief in accountability in the Hereafter. All the required deeds are the demands of the belief in accountability in the Hereafter. The first duty of a Muslim is to stand upon the truth and to suppress falsehood. He rises with goodness and ends evil. His entire activity is the worship of Allah. He turns towards Allah in every movement, and every deed必ず has its recompense. Sometimes this recompense is received in this world, but the complete recompense can be received only in the Hereafter. The final reckoning of every human being will take place in the Hereafter. Therefore the reality of the Hereafter is most logical and necessary. People must be raised so that they may give an account of their lives. When the sense of accountability in the Hereafter disappears from someone's mind, all the deeds and morals that are based on this belief vanish from that person's life. Such a person can by no means be, at the least, a Muslim.

But these people did not look at this matter from this angle. They looked at it from an entirely different angle and from a completely simple point of view. In this regard they did not reflect at all upon the reality of life and death, nor did they reflect upon any aspect of Allah's system of decree and destiny. Therefore they became believers in it.

Qur'an verse 50:3: ﴿When we have died and become dust? That is a return far-fetched.﴾

In their view, the problem is that the resurrection of life after death and after becoming dust is improbable, and this is a very simple position to hold. For once life has been placed into dead earth, what is so difficult about placing life again into the earth in the same way, when this very miracle is being enacted before them at every moment, and is occurring in every aspect of this universe? In this surah the Qur'an has drawn their attention to this point.

But before we speak about the indications of the Qur'an and the cosmic proofs concerning this exhibition-hall of life, it is appropriate that we reflect carefully upon the reference they made to dying and becoming dust, which the Qur'an has quoted and then commented upon.

﴿When we have died and become dust?﴾ (50:3)

Yes, we shall die and become dust. Whoever reads these words of the Qur'an, which the Qur'an has taken from the mouths of the disbelievers, looks upon his own self, sees the other living beings around him, and certainly reflects upon the process of death and becoming dust. Indeed, even when he is alive and walking about, he feels that perhaps the process of becoming dust has already begun in his body. In short, there is no thing other than death whose thought does not shake the human heart, and the mere thought of becoming dust in the grave makes a person tremble.

The commentary on this passage deepens the impact of what has been said. It pictures the earth gradually consuming these bodies.

Regarding ﴿Indeed, We know what the earth diminishes of them, and with Us is a Record preserved.﴾ (50:4): "We know what the earth diminishes of them, and with Us is a Book that preserves everything."

The manner of expression adopted makes the earth appear living and active, consuming the bodies that vanish gradually into its mouth. This earth consumes these bodies with great slowness. Then their bodies are shown as being consumed continuously. Whatever part of their body the earth consumes, Allah knows it, and it is being recorded what that part is. Therefore the particles of their bodies do not get lost somewhere after death. As for how the soul will be breathed back into this dust, that has already happened once. And the countless living things being created around them, which have no end, are before their eyes.

In this way the hearts are made to feel with such acute sensitivity that they melt and become soft, and within them the perception is sharpened to such a degree that they quickly accept the matter. This is done as a preface, before stating the principal matter that is the actual purpose.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 50, verse 5:

After this, their personalities are analysed and the real cause is stated, which is why they raise the same objections: they have abandoned the firm platform of truth, and there is no ground beneath their feet. For this reason they cannot stand firm on any position.

﴿Rather, they denied the truth when it came to them, so they are in a confused matter.﴾ (50:5) "Indeed, the moment the truth came to them, they plainly rejected it. That is why they are now caught in confusion."

This is also a remarkably distinctive way of expressing it. Those who constantly abandon the truth find that their feet cannot rest anywhere.

Truth is a point on which the person who believes in it is established. After that, there is no slipping in his steps. In his conduct there is no restlessness, because the ground beneath his feet is firm. There is no earthquake in him, and no part of him sinks into the earth; whereas the other people in his environment are wavering, anxious, unstable, and deprived of the wealth of certainty. Among them there is no strong character, and they cannot bear hardships. Whoever transgresses the truth and swerves this way and that, slips, and is deprived of stability and tranquillity, and will never have peace of mind. He will always remain afflicted with doubt, anxiety and restlessness.

Then, when a person abandons the truth, the storms of base desires begin to blow from every direction. Inclinations and desires, ever-changing desires, do not let him settle in one place. Bewildered and distraught, stumbling and staggering, he sometimes runs this way and sometimes that way. Wherever he stands, he is not content. Like a madman, he keeps running right, left, forward and backward. For him there is no abode of peace and tranquillity.

This is a strange manner of expression: that he is caught in "amrin marij" (a confused, disordered matter). It describes a state in which there is confusion, he is unable to decide, and he is gripped by constant unease. The manner of expression is such that his outward movements reveal his inner condition, and people can see it.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 50, verse 6:

The theme under discussion was that these people did not believe in resurrection after death and in the gathering and dispersal (hashr wa nashr). For this, it was stated that the proof sufficient for them is that the foundation of this universe is upon the truth, which is firmly established within it and appears like a towering mountain. Therefore, now certain scenes of the truth found within this universe are presented here. It is said: consider the heavens and the earth, look at the mountains firmly set in the earth, look at the rains that pour down from the sky, look at the date palms that grow tall to great heights, look at the gardens and vegetation. All of these are signs of the truth. Just as these things are lasting, the truth is also lasting. These are examples of truth expressed in a most beautiful manner.

﴿Have they not then looked at the sky above them, how We constructed it and adorned it, and that there are no flaws in it?﴾

This sky is one page of the book of this universe. This book bears witness to the truth which these people deny. Do they not see how much height, stability and permanence there is in this universe? Moreover, in these heavens there is beauty and perfection, and in their system there is no disorder or instability. Stability and perfection and beauty are attributes of the sky, and these attributes also create a harmony within the manner of expression, because truth too possesses perfection, beauty, stability and permanence. Accordingly, for the heavens are mentioned the attributes of being well-ordered, beautiful, enduring, and free from holes and cracks.

Qualities of this kind are used for the earth as well, because the earth too is one of the wonders of this universe. It possesses stability, perfection and beauty, and it has been given repose. The earth is brought into contrast with the heavens.

﴿And the earth — We spread it out, and placed firm mountains upon it, and caused to grow in it every lovely kind of plant.﴾ (50:7)

The earth being spread out, the mountains being firmly set, and the vegetation being beautiful are all things that display perfection and beauty, and at first glance these qualities are apparent. By showing them the well-built and vast heavens, the spread-out earth, and the lofty mountains, the minds and hearts of these people are directed toward one point, and that point is this.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 50, verses 8–9:

﴿تبصرة وذكرى لكل عبد منيب﴾ (50:8) "These are all things that open the eyes and give lesson, for every servant who turns (to the truth) in repentance."

These are matters that grant insight, that give sight, and that open hearts to accepting the truth. Through this contemplation the human heart, mind and soul become connected with this universe, and attain the wisdom, the training and the perfection of creation that lie within it. Then those whose hearts incline toward their Deity return after beholding the perfections of their Lord.

In this way a unity and connection comes into being between the human heart and this great and beautiful universe. Man studies the book of the universe and becomes acquainted with it, and this has an effect on the human heart and human thought. This connection and relationship affects human life, and it is this relationship that the Qur'an establishes between science, the knowledge of God (ma'rifah Ilahi), and the reality. That is, between the knowledge of God that a person possesses and the reality that scientific knowledge possesses; and in the scientific methodology of knowledge prevalent in our age this reality is absent. This relationship does not exist. Thus God created a bond between human beings and this universe in which they live, and the scholars and scientists of the modern age have severed this bond. Man is a part of this universe, and until he becomes its companion his life can neither be stable nor upright. And until there is harmony between the beat of his heart and the movement of this universe, he cannot succeed. Whatever new discoveries man makes in the stars and planets, the heavens and atmospheres, plants and animals, and in this universe and its vastness, that discovery must be in harmony with the heart. And man must become a friend of this newly discovered world, and so arrive at the conclusion that the ultimate Creator and Cause of man and this universe is Allah, the Exalted. Until knowledge, discovery and the final stage of recognition reach the stage of the Creator, that knowledge must be understood to be deficient. Every such research, and every result of such research, is barren, purposeless and useless for man.

This universe is an open book of truth, to be read in every language, and comprehended through every means. A dweller of a tent or a hut can read it, and so can the highly educated person who lives in palaces. Each person reads it according to the capacity of his perception. "Har kase az ghan-e khud shud yad-e man" (each one remembers me according to his own song). Everyone finds in it the truth according to his ability, provided he reads it with the intention of reaching truth and reality. This book stands in every state and is open before everyone.

﴿تبصرة وذكرى لكل عبد منيب﴾ (50:8) "These are all things that open the eyes and give admonition, for every person who seeks the truth." But modern scientific disciplines have been arranged in such a way that their capacity to serve as insight and to open eyes has been eliminated. The connection between the human heart and soul and this universe has been severed, because this knowledge is in the hands of those whose hearts are blind, and over whose heads a so-called scientific mode of thought rides. And this scientific approach is that the universe be cut off from the human soul.

However, the faith-based study of the universe in no way diminishes the so-called scientific approach of these people; rather, it adds to it the insight that these cosmic realities are also interconnected with one another, and that these realities are further linked with a Supreme Reality. By linking these realities with that Supreme Reality, it then joins all realities with human perception, human consciousness and the human soul in such a way that they affect a person, affect his life. These should not be mere dry information buried in minds with no purpose in practical life; rather they should influence practical life through the path of faith, and all our research and discoveries should, through the path of faith, be connected with the Supreme Reality and affect the practical life of man.

Having drawn attention to this point, the discussion now moves forward within this book of the universe, the central theme being that after death there will be resurrection, gathering and reckoning.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 50, verse 10:

The water that descends from the heavens gives life to hearts even before it gives life to the dead earth, and its descent has a very good effect upon hearts. Not only do small children rejoice in the rain, run toward it and leap and frolic in it, but also elderly people who possess a sense of beauty rejoice upon seeing the rain, and their hearts too feel joy in the rain. Children, after all, are small.

Here the rainwater is called ma' mubarak (blessed water), through which Allah produces gardens of various kinds of fruit and crops that are harvested. And through it are caused to grow tall date palms and their ripened fruit, and beautiful trees.

﴿وَالنَّخْلَ بَاسِقَاتٍ لَّهَا طَلْعٌ نَّضِيدٌ﴾ (50:10) "And tall date palms with spathes stacked one above another." The attribute tah ba tah (layered one upon another) has been used for the clusters. This adds further to the beauty of the tall tree, upon which clusters are seen hanging in layers. In terms of theme and meaning too these words are appropriate, because the discussion concerns truth and reality. Truth is elevated and beautiful, and its word too should be elevated.

And by bestowing these favours upon man, a sense of gratitude is being created in the human heart: behold this clear water, these gardens and groves, these fields and animals, and these date palms laden with fruit that reach toward the sky, all of this.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 50, verse 11:

Rizqan lil-ibad (50:11): "This is the arrangement for providing sustenance to the servants." From where does Allah bring the means of this sustenance? Then He causes vegetation to grow, then He brings forth fruits, all of this for His servants. Allah alone is the true Master, and the servants do not have the ability to give Him thanks in full.

And now, the whole universe is moving toward this goal.

Wa ahyayna bihi baldatan maytatan kadhalika al-khurooj (50:11): "And by it We give life to a dead land (so too will be the emergence of dead humans from the earth)." This process is being repeated in your environment day and night, and you have become accustomed to it. You see it, but this matter does not enter your understanding, and yet you still raise objections. If you were to reflect, your objection would seem strange to you. Just as people are being born on the present earth, with the same ease they will be raised again. The style of the Qur'an is truly magnificent: it first gives proofs and then the claim, and after a long list of various proofs and effects from the universe, it finally says "thus." And a person is greatly moved by this style.

Now from the long record of human history come some lessons and admonitions. The earlier arguments were drawn from the open book of this universe. Now turn the pages of the book of history, and see what the end of those who denied accountability in the Hereafter was. Reflect upon your own attitude. They too denied in the same way as you are denying, and the punishment that came upon them, could not such a punishment come upon you?

﴿Before them the people of Noah denied, and the companions of the Rass, and Thamud, and ʿAad, and Pharaoh, and the brothers of Lot, and the companions of the Thicket, and the people of Tubba'. Each one denied the messengers, and so My warning came due upon them.﴾ [50:12–14] ﴿Were We then weary with the first creation? Nay, they are in doubt about a new creation.﴾

Ayka means a well, a well whose walls are built of stones, and Ayka means a thicket of trees. The companions of the Ayka are most likely the people of Shu'ayb. The details of the companions of the Rass are not mentioned in the Qur'an. Tubba' is a title of the Himyarite kings. As for the other nations to which reference is made, they are well known.

It is clear that the purpose of this brief allusion is not to give the details of these nations, but only to state that they were destroyed when they denied the messengers of the Lord of the worlds. This sentence is worthy of attention.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 50, verse 14:

Each of them denied the messengers, so My warning came true against them. (50:14) This indicates that the messengers are one; the nature of their office is one, and their purpose has also been one. Yet not all of them denied all the messengers; rather, each people denied one messenger, but denying one messenger is in truth denying all of them. The messengers are all brothers, and prophethood is one lineage (shajara-e-nasab), whose roots extend deep into history, and every branch of this tree is in reality a summary of its characteristics. And it has one form: whoever abandons one branch has laid hold of the entire lineage. "So My warning came true against them" (50:14), the details of which are known to the listeners.

The divine punishment came upon these peoples because of their denial, and the denial they made was of the Resurrection, and so the question of Allah...

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 50, verse 15:

Afa'iyyina bil-khalqil-awwal (50:15): "Were We incapable of the first creation?" That is, was this evidence not before them? Since the creation was present before them, they gave no answer.

Bal hum fi labsin min khalqin jadid (50:15): "Rather, they are in doubt about a new creation." They did not look at the fact that this process is present before them. The evidence is present, so the remedy for them was exactly what was done.

Lesson No. 248: At a Glance

This is the second lesson of this surah. Here too the subject is resurrection after death, just as it was the subject of the first part. Some further effective arguments are placed before those who deny. But these arguments are in a somewhat threatening manner and consist of frightening scenes. They show that Allah is watching, as was stated at the beginning of the surah. Then the pangs of death are mentioned, then the reckoning and accounting and the presentation of everyone's record of deeds, and then Hell will open its mouth, and whenever a portion of its human fuel is thrown into it, it will lick its lips, taste it, and say:

﴿Is there any more?﴾ (50:30) "Is there anything more?"

In short, this is one single journey. It begins from creation, passes through the pangs of death, and ends at the reckoning. It is a long journey of life, connected and linked together. In this scene it is recorded in the form of continuous links, in which no link is separate from another. No one can escape from any link or stage. And man, from the beginning of this journey to its end, is in the control of Allah. At no place or stage is he free from Allah. He is at all times under Allah's supervision. The picture of this journey drawn in this surah is both frightening and astonishing: that a human being is passing through the stages of the journey in the power of Allah, the Irresistible, the Overpowering, who knows all the secrets of hearts. What can man do when the One who calls him is unique and has no partner, who neither forgets, nor sleeps, nor is heedless of anything? Even a man is greatly terrified when he senses that the intelligence service of some earthly government is following him. What would the government of the earthly people be, and what would their spies be? If some secret police are indeed keeping watch, they are watching only the outward movements of a person. He hides from that police inside his house when he enters his home and closes the door behind him, or when he shuts his mouth and does not utter a word. But the watch of Allah, the Overpowering, the Irresistible, is very strict. Wherever man is, in whatever state he is, His agents are writing at every moment, and He knows even the secrets of hearts. The truth is that Allah's watch is a stern watch.

At the beginning of the verse is:

﴿And We have indeed created man﴾ (50:16) "We have created man."

Here the intention is to point to a subsidiary meaning of this expression: that the maker of any thing, machinery or apparatus knows its reality well. Yet he is not its creator, because he did not create the material of the apparatus and machinery, and he added nothing to its formation and composition. Whereas Allah is the Creator, the Originator, and also the One who joins together the human being. This is something that has come out of the hand of power of Allah from beginning to end. Therefore He is well acquainted with this reality and its secrets and mysteries. He is aware of its past, present and final outcome.

﴿And We know what his soul whispers to him﴾ (50:16) "And We know what his inner self whispers to him." Thus man comes to know that everything about him is manifest before Allah. There is no veil between him and his Creator. The Creator is aware of the most hidden aspirations of his heart. And for the Day of Reckoning, which he denies, every kind of preparation is being made.

﴿And We are nearer to him than his jugular vein﴾ (50:16) "And We are nearer to him than his jugular vein." That is, the jugular vein through which his blood is flowing. This is a picture of Allah's possession and direct supervision. When a person contemplates this reality, his very being trembles. If a person keeps in mind only the meaning of this verse, he would never say anything that displeases Allah; rather, he would not let undesirable thoughts enter his heart. This verse alone is sufficient for a person to remain cautious at all times, to remain fearful at all times, and to remain alert at all times for the reckoning and accounting. The Holy Qur'an further explains this supervision by showing that a person's whole life, every movement, sleeping, eating, drinking, remaining silent, speaking, in short the whole journey of life, is passing between two angels. These angels sit on the right and left. They record every word as soon as it comes out of his mouth.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 50, verses 17–18:

"When the two receivers receive, one seated on the right and one on the left. Not a word does he utter but there is a watcher beside him, ready (to record)."

That is: the watcher is present and ready (ḥāḍir bāsh). ʿAtīd is an attribute of raqīb. This is not the meaning that comes to mind, namely that of two watchers one of whom is named Raqīb and the other ʿAtīd.

The question arises: how do they record? In this matter, a person should not put forward his own imaginings. These are unseen matters (ghaybī umūr), and they should be accepted in the manner in which they are mentioned in the Qur'an. We have faith in the meaning, and we do not know the modality (kayfiyyah). Even if the modality were known, there would be no benefit in it. Moreover, some modes lie beyond the sphere of our experience, and we cannot even conceive of them.

In the modern age we have seen recording methods of which our forefathers could not even conceive. By these methods every movement and every word of a human being is recorded: audio, video, tape, cinema reel, and television tape (and now computers and their networks). The scope of human recording has thus expanded. As for Allah and His agents, they may have means and methods of which we cannot yet even conceive. Just believe in what Allah has informed us.

We should live within the reality whose picture has been drawn for us, and we should renew the awareness that whatever we say and whatever act we commit, there are Allah's agents seated on our right and left, writing, so that this record may be presented against us or in our favour on the Day of Resurrection. This reckoning is such that nothing is missed from it.

We should live our lives keeping this reality fresh in our minds. This alone is sufficient for us, whether or not we know its modality. As for the question of what its modality is, that would be a futile endeavour. Those who benefited from this Qur'an, its realities, and the guidance of Muḥammad (ﷺ) followed this approach: strengthen awareness and act, and that is all.

Imam Aḥmad related from Abū Muʿāwiyah, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar ibn ʿAlqamah al-Laythī, from his father, from his grandfather, and from Bilāl ibn al-Ḥārith al-Muzanī, that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A man utters a word which is a word of Allah's pleasure, and he does not think that Allah records His pleasure because of it until the Day of Resurrection. And another man utters a word which is a cause of Allah's displeasure, and he does not realise where this word will reach. Allah records His displeasure with that person until the Day of Resurrection." It is said that ʿAlqamah used to say: "How many words there are which I have refrained from saying because of the ḥadīth of Bilāl ibn al-Ḥārith." (Tirmidhi, Nasa'i, Ibn Majah.)

It is reported from Imam Aḥmad that while he was in the throes of death (sakarāt al-mawt) he was crying out, and he heard that this cry too was being recorded, so he fell silent, and his soul departed. Thus these people took the Qur'anic guidance, and thus was their life.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 50, verses 17–18:

"When the two receivers receive, one seated on the right and one on the left. Not a word does he utter but there is a watcher beside him, ready (to record)."

That is: the watcher is present and ready (ḥāḍir bāsh). ʿAtīd is an attribute of raqīb. This is not the meaning that comes to mind, namely that of two watchers one of whom is named Raqīb and the other ʿAtīd.

The question arises: how do they record? In this matter, a person should not put forward his own imaginings. These are unseen matters (ghaybī umūr), and they should be accepted in the manner in which they are mentioned in the Qur'an. We have faith in the meaning, and we do not know the modality (kayfiyyah). Even if the modality were known, there would be no benefit in it. Moreover, some modes lie beyond the sphere of our experience, and we cannot even conceive of them.

In the modern age we have seen recording methods of which our forefathers could not even conceive. By these methods every movement and every word of a human being is recorded: audio, video, tape, cinema reel, and television tape (and now computers and their networks). The scope of human recording has thus expanded. As for Allah and His agents, they may have means and methods of which we cannot yet even conceive. Just believe in what Allah has informed us.

We should live within the reality whose picture has been drawn for us, and we should renew the awareness that whatever we say and whatever act we commit, there are Allah's agents seated on our right and left, writing, so that this record may be presented against us or in our favour on the Day of Resurrection. These are the pages of the book of life, and the last page of this worldly life is being turned.

﴿And the agony of death will come with the truth. This is what you used to flee from.﴾ (50:19)

Death is the reality that all of Allah's creatures fear, and every person tries to erase the thought of it from their mind. But how is that possible? Death is a seeker that never tires of its pursuit. It draws closer to a person at its own pace, and the pace of its steps never slows. The appointed time of death is never changed. The final moments of life, called sakarat al-mawt (the agonies of death), make a person's limbs tremble merely at the thought of them. As this scene of death is being shown on the screen, the question comes:

﴿This is what you used to flee from.﴾ (50:19) A person is still alive in this world and can hear this question. But when he is truly in the moments of the agony of death and hears this question at that time, what will his condition be?

It is reported in a hadith that when the agonies of death came upon the Prophet (ﷺ), he was wiping sweat from his blessed face and saying: "Glory be to Allah, indeed the agonies of death are truly severe." He said this even though he was journeying towards al-Rafiq al-A'la (the Highest Companion) and was longing for the liqa' (meeting) with Allah. What then will be the condition of others?

One word in this verse deserves attention:

﴿And the agony of death will come with the truth.﴾ (50:19) This shows that when a person is in his final moments, he sees the Hereafter. All veils are removed, and things he was ignorant of become known to him. Even those matters he used to deny come before him. But by then time has run out. Now seeing is of no benefit. What use is knowledge, virtue, and the perception of realities at this point? For the door of repentance has closed, and faith is no longer of benefit. This was the truth he used to deny and about which he was in great doubt. Now that he has attained it and is affirming it, this perception and affirmation are of no use to him.

The Terrors of the Reckoning on the Plain of Gathering, Just Beyond the Agonies of Death!

This is a scene such that merely refreshing it in the mind is sufficient. If a person keeps it fresh, the whole of his worldly life will be spent in caution, fear and expectation. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "How can I enjoy life, when the one with the horn has placed the horn to his mouth, lowered his forehead, and is waiting to be commanded?" The Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) said: "Then what should we say?" He (ﷺ) said: "Say: ﴿Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal-wakeel﴾ (Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs)." People then began to say: ﴿Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal-wakeel﴾. (Tirmidhi)

Surah 50, verse 21:

﴿And every soul will come, with it a driver and a witness.﴾ Each person came in such a state that with them was one who drives them along and one who bears witness. He came, the one who is being reckoned with and who is about to be punished. There is one who drives him along forcefully and one who gives testimony. It is also possible that these two are the recording angels and those who guarded him in the world. It is also possible that they are he himself and the angels. But the first explanation is the preferred one (rajih). This is the best way of presenting someone at a court, but this is the court of Allah, the Almighty (Jabbar). In such a difficult moment, this is what will be said to him.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 50, verse 22:

﴿Laqad kunta fi ghaflatin min hadha fakashafna anka ghitaaaka fa-basarukal-yawma hadid﴾ (50:22): "You were heedless of this, so We have removed from you your covering, and your sight today is sharp." Today your sight is very keen, and it sees beyond the veils. In the place of work you were negligent; you gave no thought to that time. This is the outcome you did not expect. Would that you had looked today. Today your sight is sharp.

Now his companion advances. The preferred view is that this is the witness who has his record of deeds.

[Qur'an 50:23] "And his companion will say: 'This is what is ready with me.'" ... 

Actually, I need to produce the translation as requested, without the stray bracket above. Here it is:

"His companion [the recording angel] will say: 'This is what is ready with me.' ('Atid means present and ready; that is, nothing new is being prepared now, it is already ready.

Here the record is no longer read out, so a decree is issued from the court swiftly and is carried into effect. Immediately from the presence of the Lord of Honour, the one who drove and the witness are commanded."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 50, verses 24–26:

أَلْقِيَا فِي جَهَنَّمَ كُلَّ كَفَّارٍ عَنِيدٍ (50:24) مَنَّاعٍ لِلْخَيْرِ مُعْتَدٍ مُرِيبٍ (50:25) الَّذِي جَعَلَ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلَهًا آخَرَ فَأَلْقِيَاهُ فِي الْعَذَابِ الشَّدِيدِ (50:26) "Cast into Hell every stubborn disbeliever, who withheld from good, transgressed, and was in doubt, who set up another god with Allah; so cast him into severe punishment."

By mentioning these attributes, the fear and terror of those who are already caught in the difficulties of that hard time increase further, because a dread of the wrath of Allah, the Almighty and the Subduer, arises over the criminals who are already in trouble. All these attributes deserve that the criminal be given the greatest possible punishment: a stubborn disbeliever, one who harbours enmity, who prevents every good, who exceeds bounds in every matter, and who is extremely doubtful, and who has set up other deities alongside Allah. After enumerating these attributes comes the emphatic command: فَأَلْقِيَاهُ فِي الْعَذَابِ الشَّدِيدِ (50:26) "cast him into severe punishment", meaning into the punishment of Hell, which will indeed be severe.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 50, verses 27–29:

At this point, they too are overcome with fear and tremble, and they hastily reject any shadow of accusation against themselves, merely on the ground that this person was a companion of the one destined for Hell.

﴿Qarīnuhu qāla rabbanā mā aṭghaytuhu wa-lākin kāna fī ḍalālin baʿīd﴾ (50:27): "His companion said: 'Our Lord, I did not make him rebellious; rather, he was himself in far-off error.'" It is possible that this companion is not the one mentioned earlier, who presented the record of this criminal. Rather, what is meant may be the devil who was assigned to him, to lead him astray. And now he is occupied with disowning himself here. The whole Qur'an contains such scenes and dialogues in which the misleading devils are seen disowning their followers, as is the case here, so this too is not beyond possibility. But it is also possible that the "companion" (qarīn) means the angel who prepared the record of deeds, and who, frightened by this dreadful divine judgment, is expressing his disassociation and stating: "Indeed, I was the companion of this wretched one, but I had no hand in their misguidance." In this way, the disowning by this exonerated person of his own innocence indicates that, on seeing this frightful and anguishing scene, the companion-angel spoke thus.

Now the final decision comes, and the matter is concluded:

﴿Qāla lā takhtaṣimū ladayya wa-qad qaddamtu ilaykum bil-waʿīd. Mā yubaddalu l-qawlu ladayya wa-mā anā biẓallāmin lil-ʿabīd﴾ (50:28–29): "He will say: 'Do not dispute in My presence, for I had already sent you warning in advance of the consequence. The word is not changed with Me, and I am not one who wrongs His servants.'"

Therefore, this is not a place for disputing. You were repeatedly warned beforehand that every deed would be met with reward or punishment, and all deeds have been recorded. Now no change in them is possible. Everyone will receive recompense according to their record of deeds. No one will be wronged, because the Judge who rewards is just.

With this, the scene of reckoning ends in all its terrors and intensity, but this discussion has not yet concluded, for a further frightening aspect of it still remains.

This entire scene is a scene of question and answer; here Hell is presented as a party to a dialogue, which makes it a strange and frightening picture. All the disbelievers are present: the obstinate, those who prevent good, those who transgress limits, and those who doubt the Hereafter. They are being thrown into Hell in great numbers, and heaps of them accumulate in it. After this, Hell is addressed: "Are you filled?" and "Are these people sufficient for you?" But it will answer harshly, boiling with rage and blazing:

*Hal min mazid* (50:30) (Is there anything more?), in the manner of a ravenous, ferocious beast that opens its mouth wide. What a frightening scene this is!

The Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 50, verse 31:

On the other side there is another beautiful scene: a love in which everyone is pleased, all the God-fearing (muttaqun) gathered in one place, Paradise brought near to them, and cries of "Marhaba, marhaba" (welcome, welcome) on every side.

﴿And Paradise will be brought near to the God-fearing, not far away.﴾ (50:31) ﴿This is what you were promised, for every one who turns back (to Allah) often and guards (His limits) carefully, who fears the Most Merciful unseen and comes with a heart turned in repentance. Enter it in peace. That is the Day of Eternal Life.﴾ (50:32-34) ﴿For them therein is whatever they wish, and with Us is more.﴾ (50:35)

In the dialogue of this scene, every word carries honour and dignity. Paradise is brought near to the people of faith. Therefore they do not have to undertake any journey to reach it; rather, Paradise itself comes walking to their feet.

ghair ba'eed (50:31): "not far away." And apart from other blessings, there will be the pleasure of Allah, and it will be said...

This is what you were promised, for every one who turned back (to Allah) in repentance and guarded (his limits) with care, who feared the Most Merciful though unseen, and who came with a heart turned in devotion.

Thus, from the higher realm, their praise is pronounced, and it is said that by Allah's measure they are those who turn back to Him and guard their souls thoroughly; they fear the Most Merciful (al-Rahman) though they never saw Him. Their hearts are attached to Allah, and they are obedient to His command.

This is the commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 50, verse 34:

After this, an announcement is made that you should enter Paradise in peace, and that you will never have to leave it.

"Enter it in peace; that is the Day of Eternity" (50:34). "Enter Paradise in peace." That day will be the day of everlasting life.

Then, in the higher realm, an announcement will be made to honour them: these are the people for whom, with their Lord, there is much more, and that is without limit.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 50, verse 35:

﴿Lahum ma yashā'ūna fīhā wa-ladaynā mazīd﴾ (50:35) "There they will have whatever they wish, and with Us there is yet more."

They cannot reach the limit of Allah's bounties no matter how much they wish, and what Allah has in store as "more" is boundless.

This is the last lesson of this surah. It is, as it were, a final thunderous call, announced with great force: listen to what has happened to the earlier nations in human history. It contains a glimpse of the cosmos, presents a scene concerning resurrection and gathering, and gives guidance about the Quran, that you should continue your work. There are also many instructions for the heart and sight in this lesson.

All these glimpses have passed through this entire surah as well, but at the end they are repeated with a fresh touch. The same points are repeated rapidly and point by point, but in a new taste and a new style, and this is the miraculous quality of the Quran: when it repeats a matter within a single surah, it appears new.

Earlier it was said:

﴿Before them the people of Noah, the companions of the Rass, and Thamud denied, and ʿAd and Pharaoh and the brothers of Lot, and the companions of the Thicket and the people of Tubba'. Each denied the messengers, and so My warning came due against them﴾ (50:12–14).

And here it is said:

The reality to which indication was intended is this, but here it is in a completely new style, and quite different from the manner of the first verse. Here an additional attribute of these nations has been added: that they had dug tunnels through the whole world and searched it thoroughly. They ran about everywhere, seeking the means of life. But when they were seized, was there then any way of escape?

﴿Then was there any place of refuge for them?﴾ (50:36). No! Here is an addition which makes the matter even more vivid:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 50, verse 37:

There is a very great lesson in the rise and fall of past nations, but it is only for the person who possesses a heart and a mind. The history of nations cannot move a heart that is dead; or else that person does not possess a heart and mind at all. Rather, for taking admonition and drawing a lesson, it is sufficient that a person quietly listens to the story of the rise and fall of nations. This story will explain itself. The truth is that this is a great reality. The stories of past nations have a very great effect on the human soul. In this regard, even a slight awakening and a slight openness of the heart are enough to be affected by memories and reflections, and it has a great impact on a person, and many changes come about in him.

Before this, a page of the book of this universe had been turned over:

﴿Have they not looked at the sky above them, how We constructed it and adorned it, and it has no flaws? And the earth — We spread it out, and placed firm mountains in it, and caused to grow in it every beautiful species of plant.﴾ (50:6–7)

And here it is thus.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 50, verse 38:

﴿Surely We created the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them in six days, and no weariness touched Us.﴾ (50:38)

So, here a further truth is added to the first point.

﴿And no weariness touched Us.﴾ (50:38) The purpose here is to show that Allah created this vast universe with great ease. Raising the dead is no great matter; compared with those awe-inspiring heavens, it is a very small task. A further guidance, as a lesson.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 50, verses 39–40:

﻿"So be patient over what they say, and glorify your Lord with praise before the rising of the sun and before its setting. And glorify Him during part of the night and at the ends of the prostrations." (50:39–40)

"Therefore, O Prophet, be patient over what these people say, and continue to glorify your Lord with His praise, glorifying Him before the rising of the sun and before its setting, and at night glorify Him, and also after you have finished your prostrations."

The rising and setting of the sun, and the scene of night after sunset, are all connected with the scenes and movements of the heavens and the earth. Glorification, praise, bowing and prostration have been linked with them, and the instruction is given to be patient over the words of these people, because they deny the unjust resurrection and gathering and the giving of life again. Here, as it were, something new has been introduced into the recurrence of night and day. Praise, glorification, bowing and prostration have also been connected with the scenes of this universe. Thus, whenever bowing and prostration take place, these cosmic scenes will also be before our eyes: the scenes of the sun's rising and setting and the coming of night.

﻿"So be patient over what they say, and glorify your Lord with praise before the rising of the sun and before its setting. And glorify Him during part of the night and at the ends of the prostrations." (50:39–40)

"Therefore, O Prophet, be patient over what these people say, and continue to glorify your Lord with His praise, glorifying Him before the rising of the sun and before its setting, and at night glorify Him, and also after you have finished your prostrations."

The rising and setting of the sun, and the scene of night after sunset, are all connected with the scenes and movements of the heavens and the earth. Glorification, praise, bowing and prostration have been linked with them, and the instruction is given to be patient over the words of these people, because they deny the unjust resurrection and gathering and the giving of life again. Here, as it were, something new has been introduced into the recurrence of night and day. Praise, glorification, bowing and prostration have also been connected with the scenes of this universe. Thus, whenever bowing and prostration take place, these cosmic scenes will also be before our eyes: the scenes of the sun's rising and setting and the coming of night.

This is another theme linked to the pages of this universe. That is: be patient, glorify (your Lord), and prostrate, while you (ﷺ) await a great event and a momentous occurrence, which can come at any time in the turning of night and day. Only those whose hearts are drowned in heedlessness can be unaware of it. And this is the pillar and axis of this surah, and its true subject.

﴿And listen, [O Muhammad], on the day the caller calls from a place near. The day they will hear the Shout in truth. That is the Day of Coming Out [of the graves]. Indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and to Us is the final return. The Day the earth will split apart from them, [and they will rush out] hastening. That is a gathering which is easy for Us.﴾ (50:41–44)

This is a new and impactful scene: the scene of a day that will be very difficult. It is expressed in another place in a different manner:

﴿And the Horn will be blown. That is the Day of the Threat. And every soul will come, with it a driver and a witness.﴾ (50:20–21)

Here, along with the blowing of the Horn, there is also mention of a cry, and with it the scene of coming out appears. Then the earth is splitting open and people are coming forth from it. All the creatures who were buried in this earth from the beginning of life to the end of this journey will emerge. All these graves will burst open, and whoever and however many were buried in them will come out. Ma'arri says:

How many a grave has become a grave again and again,
Laughing at the clash of opposites [buried within it].
One buried upon the remains of another buried,
Over long ages and vast periods of time.

(How many graves there are, which have been made into graves repeatedly; they are laughing at the varied kinds of people who have been buried within them. One dead person is buried upon the remains of another, over long and ancient times.)

After the earth splits, everything will come out on its own: broken bodies, bones, particles that are in the atmosphere of the earth or have been carried by flowing water into the valleys, wherever they have come to rest, whose place only Allah knows. They will all gather together. This is a scene beyond the grasp of our imagination.

In the shadow of this impactful scene, the reality they used to deny is being brought forward.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 50, verse 43:

إنا نحن نحيي ونميت وإلينا المصير (50:43) "It is We who give life and cause death, and to Us is the final return." And:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 50, verse 44:

﴿That is a gathering upon Us, easy.﴾ (50:44) And this was the most fitting time and place for the expression of this truth.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 50, verse 45:

Under the shade of this scene, the Prophet (ﷺ) is instructed to continue his work steadfastly. He should not care about their disputes and quarrels, their obstinacy and their denial. The truth that is being presented before them is clear, and if one has insight, it can be seen.

﴿We know best what they say, and you are not a compeller over them. So remind, by the Qur'an, whoever fears My warning.﴾ (50:45) "O Prophet (ﷺ), We know well what these people are saying, and your task is not to force them to accept the message. Just admonish, through this Qur'an, everyone who fears My warning."

"We know well what they are saying": this alone is sufficient to console you, that We know, and our knowing has consequences too. This is a very frightening threat.

﴿And you are not over them a compeller﴾ (50:45): that is, you have no authority to compel anyone to faith and affirmation. The authority lies with Us. We are watching over them and are responsible for them.

﴿So remind, by the Qur'an, whoever fears My warning﴾ (50:45): the Qur'an by itself is a mighty force. It shakes hearts and sets off an earthquake in the intellectual world. No hard-hearted person can stand before it. Facing the truths of the Qur'an requires great courage. The Qur'an has a wondrous effect.

When such surahs are present for people to recite and to present, what need is there for a compeller who would twist people's necks to make them Muslims? The Qur'an possesses a power that great tyrants do not have. Through it, blows can strike hearts that cannot be inflicted by the whips of dictators and tyrants (... al-Azim).
